# Climate Change & Post-Harvey NFIP Policy Participation

Using census tract level estimates of Hurricane Harvey's flood impacts, I investigated whether neighborhoods experiencing a greater proportion of flooding attributable to climate change subsequently showed different patterns of NFIP policy uptake, renewals, and cancellations.

The analysis combined climate impact attribution data with NFIP policy information and tract-level socioeconomic and housing characteristics. Using spatial statistical models, I analyzed whether greater exposure to climate change-attributable flooding was associated with changes in post-Harvey flood insurance uptake and how these relationships varied across communities.

The analysis provided evidence that climate-attributable flooding was associated with distinct post-disaster NFIP participation outcomes—and that these outcomes diverged by neighborhood income.
